Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

loud adjective and adverb

of a voice or sound

also loudly, louder, out loud, in a loud voice, a loud voice

classical

Cic. Clu. 134: clārā vōce (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 342

clārus, clāra, clārum

Declension on Wiktionary

loud, clear (of a voice or sound)

Of sound, clear and loud at once: vōx clāra, clāmor clārus (Plaut.). In speaking loudly is clārā vōce or magnā vōce, or the adverb clārē; louder, clārius. The word’s other senses are bright and famous.

Other words

  • magnā vōce — loudly, in a loud voice

    phrase · also used · classical · Phaedr. App. 16: vōce magnā; Traupman 342

    Magnus of a voice is loud (see big).

  • clārē — loudly, clearly

    adverb · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.36.3: clārē et intentē … legō; Traupman 342 · Wiktionary

Examples

  • asellus nōtum proximum tēctum subit et vōce magnā sēsē vēnisse indicat

    the donkey goes into the nearest house he knows and announces in a loud voice that he has comePhaedr. App. 16

  • et exclāmāvērunt vōce magnā: «ipse fēcit nōs»

    and they cried out in a loud voice, “He made us”Aug. Conf. 10.6.9

See also noisy, in a low voice, lower your voice, read aloud, laugh out loud.
